messages:
sara: :rotating_light: seeing a spike in 502/504 for hosted inference since the 09:00 canary rollout. Dashboard shows API gateway errors and higher p95 latency.

mike: can you paste the dashboard? which model route?

sara: route: /v1/generate (redwood-codex-v1), errors started ~09:05 after staged rollout to 5%. 502 rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8%.

jordan: I see increased 502s correlated with canary instances added to pool. CPU fine but the gateway logs show upstream "connection reset by peer" and some 504s.

lexi: Support received multiple customer tickets about timeouts and failed requests, ticket #INC-9876 linked here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9876

nate: quick repro (from curl) returns 502 with empty body for some requests:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hey"}' -i
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nServer: gateway\nContent-Length: 0
```

sara: thanks. I also noticed the canary config had kvcache_prefetch enabled and a routing tag mismatch in the deploy metadata. suspect KV cache warmup causing backend to drop connections under certain sequence lengths.

jordan: looking at canary instance logs: worker crashes with oom-ish traces? not classic OOM but alloc failure in attention kernel during first long-context request. sequence length distribution shows a spike from a customer batch ~4096 tokens.

mike: was quantization/profile changed in this rollout?

deploy-bot: deploy v3.14.2-canary started by @sara at 09:00 (image: inference-runtime:v3.14.2, flags: kvcache_prefetch=true, enable_fast_attention=true)

nate: flag list doesn't match what dedicated tests ran against. enable_fast_attention was supposed to be off for that model until further perf verification. looks like a flag leak in the canary config.

lexi: customers reporting billing double-counts for retried requests because frontend retries on 502 then charge shows duplicate tokens. that's escalating.

sara: immediate plan: remove canary from routing and rollback the flag. Mike / Jordan can we coordinate rollback + sticky routing to avoid cascading traffic?

mike: on it. I'll pin traffic back to stable pool and scale stable by +10% to absorb load. doing: `orchestrator route update --set-canary=0 --route /v1/generate`

jordan: prepping rollback: `kubectl rollout undo rs/inference-v3 --to-revision=stable-20240315` and will remove kvcache_prefetch from the configmap. will also disable enable_fast_attention.

sara: Nate, after rollback we'll need to run targeted repro with the customer payload to validate no 502s and that retries are idempotent (billing wise).

nate: got a repro harness ready. running batch with seq=4096 to the stable pool now and verifying token accounting.

deploy-bot: rollback started by @jordan at 09:18. Canary instances draining.

mike: routing flip done. traffic baseline back to stable. monitoring p95 and 5xx.

nate: initial results: 5xx dropped from 8% -> 0.4% within 3 minutes. token counts look stable for retried requests (no duplicate billing).

lexi: I'm updating the customers in INC-9876: brief postmortem and ETA on permanent fix. will include steps to avoid duplicate charges and advise on retry logic.

sara: follow-ups: 1) roll forward a fixed runtime with disabled fast_attention and controlled kvcache_prefetch behavior; 2) add deploy-time validation that model profiles match allowed flag sets; 3) add a canary traffic gate to prevent >1% customer traffic until smoke tests pass.

mike: +1. also add an alert for sudden 5xx increase when canary traffic changes.

jordan: collecting logs and core dumps to file share for research. will attach to INC-9876.

nate: post-rollback telemetry: p50/p95 latency stable, errors back to normal. closing incident once support confirms customer communication.

lexi: customers notified. marking as "customer impacted - billing" and prepping billing audit for impacted window.

sara: thanks everyone. write up action items in the postmortem template and assign owners. :thumbsup:
